candidate.name: warm-4-256
candidate.status: opt-in; the 5.0 default (batchDeals 1) is unchanged unless the rule below is met

choiceRationale: Development round 2 (deal-weighted): the only candidate whose early control ratios stayed near 1 (river3 0.01 s 1.01, parallel64 1.85) while keeping parallel64-like equal-time ratios at 0.3-1 s on flop6/flop6w. Round 1 (update-count weighting) failed everywhere and motivated deal weighting.

seeds.justification: Development paired SD of ln(NashConv ratio) at the primary budgets was 0.35-0.55. With SD 0.45, n = ((1.96+0.84)*0.45/ln(1/0.80))^2 = 32; 40 seeds leave room for Holm over four comparisons and for seeds excluded outside observed ranges. A 10% effect would need about 160 seeds, which is why the minimum meaningful improvement is 20%.

primaryMetric: Paired mean of ln(NashConv warm-4-256 / NashConv default) at equal training wall time, exact best response by the same evaluator (mwcli --gain method=exact), log-log interpolation inside observed ranges, out-of-range seeds excluded and counted (never clamped).
promotionRule: Promote warm-4-256 to default only if (a) at flop6@1 and flop6w@1 the ratio estimate is <= 0.80 and the Holm-adjusted p (over the four primaries) is < 0.05 with ratio < 1, (b) no primary estimate is > 1, and (c) every control comparison (river3-chip and turn4, every budget, equal time) has a 95% upper bound <= 1.15 (non-inferiority margin 15%). Budgets where more than 25% of seeds are excluded are reported but do not count toward (c).
secondary: warm-4-256 vs parallel64 at equal time
per-seat gains, deals, committed updates, training time, evaluation time, peak RSS
note: NashConv here is the sum of seat gains inside each abstraction, not exploitability of the full game.
